# docker-disk

Mount an external disk under Docker's data root and restore the iptables rules Docker needs afterwards. Linux only — this uses mount -t UUID=, iptables-restore, and systemd.

---

## `docker_mount_data_disk`

Mount the configured data disk by UUID, replay Docker's saved iptables rules, and restart the docker service.

**Usage**

```sh
docker_mount_data_disk [uuid]
```

**Examples**

```sh
docker_mount_data_disk
docker_mount_data_disk 8a741529-d1f6-4c90-9f90-9dc96cddf9fc
```

**Requires** `docker`, `mount`

**OS** Linux only &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/linux/docker-disk.sh:50`](../../modules/linux/docker-disk.sh#L50)

**See also** `docker_unmount_data_disk`

---

## `docker_unmount_data_disk`

Stop docker and unmount the configured data disk.

> **⚠ DANGER** — Stops the docker daemon, killing every running container. Prompts first.

**Usage**

```sh
docker_unmount_data_disk
```

**Examples**

```sh
docker_unmount_data_disk
```

**Requires** `docker`, `umount`

**OS** Linux only &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/linux/docker-disk.sh:100`](../../modules/linux/docker-disk.sh#L100)

**See also** `docker_mount_data_disk`
